meaning: Collections of an official publisher that the publisher_tables line turns into data table packages: each names the publisher, the hosts it is read from, the exact addresses on those hosts, the licence rule bound to the exact series or release with its evidence address, and the expected shape. Licence texts are the legal code at the address of the licence's own steward, and an attribution links the licence's deed.

un_sdg_global_database.title: Global SDG Indicators Database
un_sdg_global_database.reason: UNdata's terms of use, read on October 5, 2026, say that its data 'may be copied freely, duplicated and further distributed provided that UNdata is cited as the reference'. That permission is not a licence on the owner's allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, Unlicense), so no series is read; whether such terms may be added is the owner's decision. World Development Indicators series and Our World in Data charts whose every origin is CC BY 4.0 cover many of the same indicators; Our World in Data marks origins it takes from UN agencies '(c) United Nations' (UNEP, UNFPA and WTO in the October 5 debug run), and the line refuses those charts by name.

faostat.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
faostat.title: FAOSTAT bulk downloads
faostat.reason: The bulk manifest, read on October 5, 2026, lists 69 datasets and names no licence for any of them; FAO's database terms are a general statement with exceptions for third-party data, which binds no licence to a dataset's exact bytes. The files are also large: only 4 of the 69 list fewer than 15,000 rows, about what the 2 MiB package bound holds. Held until FAO states a licence for each dataset; FAO data that the World Bank republishes under CC BY 4.0 (forest area, cereal yield, undernourishment) is supplied through World Development Indicators.

world_bank_wdi.title: World Development Indicators

licence.reason: The World Bank states a licence per series in the series' own metadata (License_Type, with License_URL); a series the dataset terms leave to a third party carries that party's terms there instead (SIPRI terms, CC BY 3.0 IGO). Only the exact value mapped here passes; any other value refuses the series with the value it found.

licence.statement: All data, visualizations, and code produced by Our World in Data are completely open access under the Creative Commons BY license
licence.reason: Our World in Data licenses its own work CC BY 4.0, which each chart page states with a link to the CC BY 4.0 deed, and says that third-party data stays under each provider's own licence. Each indicator's metadata names every origin with that origin's licence; a chart passes only when every origin of every indicator in it states CC BY 4.0 exactly and the publisher does not mark the indicator non-redistributable. Any other licence (CC BY 3.0 IGO, CC BY-NC-SA, OGL, a copyright notice, CC0 until its text travels) refuses the chart with the names found.
